main_topics.reason: The user opened by asking what POTS means and returned to its cause, outlook, and management throughout the chat.
The user asked what they could do and engaged with several suggestions, including fluids, salt, compression, and pacing activity.
The user described a pounding heart, dizziness, lightheadedness, and spotty vision when standing.
The user directly asked whether POTS meant their heart was damaged and said this was frightening.
The user asked why POTS followed long COVID after previously being healthy.
The user asked whether POTS would be permanent or whether people get better.
The user said exertion led to crashes lasting days and that exercise advice had made them feel they were failing.
The user asked whether they should be taking medication after the doctor had not prescribed any.
The user asked what to do in the moment when their heart races after standing because it feels scary.
The user said the doctor explained the diagnosis quickly and they did not understand it at first.

output.summary: The user sought an explanation of a new POTS diagnosis after long COVID, describing heart racing and dizziness on standing and asking about prognosis and management. The assistant discussed general self-management, cautioned that activity should account for the user's post-exertional crashes, and suggested discussing specifics with the care team; the user said they felt less panicked and found the information useful.
